extent.lisp:851-867: fnn-extent-entry-fresh is documented 'Extent lock held' and performs `(fnn-extent-read-entry file eoff elen)` plus the digest check. Owner-mutex holders take the same lock: fnn-owner-cold-ready-p (4312), fnn-owner-cold-result-locked (4276), and fnn-snapshot-source-root-release (4884-4885). The cold-read design (extent.lisp:883-886) says 'The pread runs WITHOUT the realizer's lock, so a stalled disk holds only this thread'.
fix: Use the issue/complete split fnn-extent-issue-read uses: take the lock to admit and find the descriptor, pread and verify without it, then retake it to settle. Or route these reads through the cold-read worker.
reviewer: owner.lisp:4963-4965 calls fnn-extent-entry-fresh under *fnn-extent-lock*. extent.lisp:851-881 shows it does the pread (fnn-extent-read-entry) and the digest check with the lock held. Owner-mutex holders take that lock: fnn-owner-cold-ready-p (4312), fnn-owner-cold-result-locked (4276) and fnn-snapshot-source-root-release (4884-4885). This contradicts the off-lock pread design at extent.lisp:883-886. Impact is limited because the frame was just written by the same publication and is normally in the page cache, so this mostly matters on a stalled device.
scenario: After every durable publication, release-extents rereads each payload frame (up to +fnn-checkpoint-batch-octets+ each) under the extent lock. Meanwhile the accept loop's fnn-owner-cold-reap, or any quantum settling a cold read, holds the owner mutex and blocks on the extent lock, so the whole owner (every reader and poster) stalls for the frame I/O. On a slow or stalled device the node freezes for the duration of the release, which the cold-read design avoids.
title: Checkpoint frames are pread and digested while holding *fnn-extent-lock*, which owner-mutex holders wait on
